_comment: Technology (scripts/sim/technology.gd Technology; DESIGN_LIVING_WORLD.md M5). Six branches of three tiers, about 30 techs. Each tech is published to the world by its R&D company in its year (plus some months, from the seed) and can then be licensed for a fee (licence: a share of the company's fleet at list price, at least floor); a company the R&D company likes (rnd_likes at or over early_at) is offered it early_months before at early_price of the fee. A company can develop a tech itself (cost in research points, from its research ships' points and a monthly budget at point_cost a point, faster with the CTO's Engineering and a Technology centre); finished before the world publishes it, it holds the tech exclusively for exclusive_years (royalties a month from the rivals who must license it) and the world's publication waits. effect: a perk (stat fuel/speed/wear/breakdowns/dock as a factor, for every ship or only categories) applies to the whole fleet at once; an upgrade (a part and its effects, above the stock upgrade) is fitted ship by ship in drydock (cost: a share of the ship's list price), and new ships ordered after come with it. Names are inventions.

techs.name: Electronic common-rail injection
techs.text: Fuel metered by the stroke: a cleaner, thriftier burn.

techs.name: Two-stage turbocharging
techs.text: Two turbochargers in series: more air, less fuel, cooler running.

techs.name: Engine condition monitoring
techs.text: Sensors on every bearing and cylinder, read ashore: faults caught before they stop a ship.

techs.name: Dual-fuel engines
techs.text: Engines that burn gas as happily as oil: the cheaper of the two, wherever the ship is.

techs.name: LNG-ready designs
techs.text: Container ships and gas carriers built to bunker gas from the start.

techs.name: Silicone foul-release coatings
techs.text: A hull too slippery for barnacles: less drag year after year.

techs.name: Hull cleaning programme
techs.text: Divers and crawlers scrubbing hulls at every long stop.

techs.name: Fatigue-tolerant structures
techs.text: Plating and frames designed round the cracks that come with age.

techs.name: Air lubrication
techs.text: A carpet of bubbles under the flat of the bottom: the hull rides on air.

techs.name: Bow optimisation
techs.text: Bows shaped by computation for the speeds ships really sail at.

techs.name: Controllable-pitch propellers
techs.text: Blades that turn to the load: the right pitch at every speed.

techs.name: Twisted rudders
techs.text: A rudder twisted to the propeller's wash: less drag, better steering.

techs.name: Hull form speed refinements
techs.text: Stern and skeg shapes that give the propeller cleaner water.

techs.name: Contra-rotating propellers
techs.text: Two propellers on one shaft turning against each other: the second recovers what the first throws away.

techs.name: Magnetic shaft bearings
techs.text: A shaft that floats in a magnetic field: nothing to wear.

techs.name: Port call planning
techs.text: Berths, cranes and gangs booked before the ship is in sight.

techs.name: Fast hatch covers
techs.text: Hydraulic covers open in minutes instead of an hour.

techs.name: Vacuum mooring
techs.text: Suction pads instead of lines: alongside in minutes, no gang on the quay.

techs.name: Twin-lift cranes
techs.text: Cranes lifting two loads at once.

techs.name: Automated terminal handling
techs.text: Ships talking to the terminal's machines: every stop choreographed.

techs.name: Fast ramps
techs.text: Wider, steeper, faster ramps for the car and boat carriers.

techs.name: Fleet tracking
techs.text: Every ship on a screen ashore: stops planned to the hour.

techs.name: Integrated bridge systems
techs.text: One console for the whole bridge: fewer wrong switches thrown.

techs.name: Weather routing
techs.text: Courses laid round the weather, not through it.

techs.name: Solid-state radars
techs.text: Radars with no magnetron to burn out.

techs.name: Predictive maintenance
techs.text: Every sensor's history read by machines that know what a failing pump sounds like.

techs.name: Trim optimisation
techs.text: Ballast shifted so the ship sits just right for her speed.

techs.name: Battery peak-shaving
techs.text: Batteries that take the peaks so the generators can idle.

techs.name: Slow-steaming optimiser
techs.text: The speed that spends the least fuel for the schedule, worked out for every leg.

techs.name: Biofuel blending
techs.text: Fuel systems that take blends of waste oils and bio-diesel.

techs.name: Wind-assist rotors
techs.text: Spinning rotor sails on the deck of the bulk carriers and tankers: the wind pays for a part of every voyage.
